tldr: An Oct 22 paper (HERD) framed continual learning as a trade-off between parametric methods, which forget, and non-parametric ones. Three days later a benchmark began measuring whether LLM agents actually improve from experience over long horizons.
whats_new: CAMR (Oct 27) proposes compatibility-aware memory replay, deciding whether incoming data is worth replaying before it is used to update an LLM.
why_it_matters: Agents that learn from experience need retention without regressions; replay selection and long-horizon evals are the pieces to watch before trusting self-improving setups.

status.detail: Three arXiv papers in six days; all research-stage, none shipped in a product.

beats.headline: HERD targets forgetting with recursive distillation
beats.summary: Positions parametric methods against catastrophic forgetting and loss of plasticity.

beats.headline: Continual Learning Exam benchmarks LLM agents over long horizons
CAMR selects what to replay by compatibility

open_questions: Do any labs report results on the Continual Learning Exam benchmark?
Do HERD or CAMR release code or reproducible numbers on production-scale models?
take_for_builders: Treat these as research signals: do not adopt, but add a retention check to any fine-tune or agent-memory pipeline that updates on new data.
